subject: LLM fit evaluation and prioritization plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@acme.ai>, Jorge Morales <procure@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: LLM fit evaluation and prioritization plan

Hi Lena / Jorge —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + recommended next steps from our side so we’re all aligned on a short, pragmatic evaluation that will answer your two top questions: quality fit for chat + reranking, and predictable unit economics.

Summary of candidate model variants we recommend evaluating (attached: acme_benchmark_summary_v1.csv, acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl):
- Variant A — Redwood-Open-7B-quant (4-bit): best cost profile, strong reranking on short contexts; expected 1-token latency improvement ~20% vs baseline.
- Variant B — Redwood-13B-std: higher quality for multi-turn chat and instruction-following; latency + cost moderate.
- Variant C — Community-70B-8k (sparse attention): top quality on long-context generation but higher inference cost; consider only if you need long-form summaries.

Tradeoffs (short):
- Cost: A << B << C (per-1k-token cost estimate included in the CSV).
- Latency: A (best) → B (mid) → C (worst) on CPU/GPU baseline we used.
- Quality: C (best on long-form), B (best multi-turn coherence), A (good for classification/rerank).

Proposed evaluation plan (3 weeks):
1) Week 0 (this week): exchange prompt set + sample user traffic (we have the prompt_set_v1 attached).
2) Week 1: Redwood runs controlled benchmarks (latency, cost, top-k rerank precision) — we’ll share per-route perf dashboards.
3) Week 2: You run a small shadow test behind a feature flag (5% traffic) to validate quality on live traffic.
4) Week 3: Decision review: recommend model + deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).

Success criteria (proposed):
- Chat: maintain NPS-style quality bucket >= 85% on curated prompts.
- Rerank: top-1 precision >= 72% on labeled set.
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms for short-turns (chat), p95 <= 450ms for rerank flows.

Action items we need from Acme by Wed 26 May:
- Sample payload (anonymized) or permission to use the prompt set against synthetic traffic.
- Procurement timeline (Jorge) and any required contract terms to start a 90-day eval.

I attached the benchmark CSV and the prompt set. I’ve also included a short SSO/checklist PDF for the private deploy route.

If this plan looks reasonable I’ll schedule the internal technical deep-dive and assign owners for the benchmark runs.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_benchmark_summary_v1.csv (summary metrics), acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (30 canonical prompts), redwood_sso_checklist.pdf (private deploy prerequisites)
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@acme.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Morales <procure@acme.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LLM fit evaluation and prioritization plan

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and the timeline fits our internal window. A couple quick clarifications before we sign off on the 3-week eval:

- For the latency numbers you mentioned, are those measured on an A100-style GPU? We run inference in us-west on DGX nodes; p95 numbers are our gating metric.
- Can you give a rough $/1k-token estimate for Variant A vs B (ballpark is fine for procurement)?
- For rerank: we’ll share a labeled sample of ~500 queries; will that be enough to hit the precision gate you listed?

Jorge: timeline from procurement side — can you confirm whether we can get PO within 30 days if the eval shows a good fit?

Lena
Director, Product
Acme.ai

On Sat, May 22, 2027 at 4:03 PM Lena Ortiz <lena@acme.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and the timeline fits our internal window. A couple quick clarifications before we sign off on the 3-week eval:
> - For the latency numbers you mentioned, are those measured on an A100-style GPU? We run inference in us-west on DGX nodes; p95 numbers are our gating metric.
> - Can you give a rough $/1k-token estimate for Variant A vs B (ballpark is fine for procurement)?
> - For rerank: we’ll share a labeled sample of ~500 queries; will that be enough to hit the precision gate you listed?

Good questions — short answers below: 
- Latency baseline: numbers in the CSV were collected on an A100 equivalent. We’ll re-run the three candidate configs on a DGX-style instance in us-west for a direct comparison and include p50/p95/p99.
- Ballpark cost per 1k tokens (in hosted mode, USD): Variant A ~ $0.08 / 1k tokens, Variant B ~ $0.22 / 1k tokens, Variant C ~ $0.55 / 1k tokens. If you plan dedicated/reserved capacity, we can give lower committed rates; I’ll include a committed estimate in the procurement pack.
- Labeled sample: 500 queries is a solid start for a precision sanity check; we’ll report confidence intervals and recommend expanding to 1k if results are borderline.

Next steps from Redwood: I’ll schedule the technical deep-dive (30–45m) early next week to sync infra specs and SSO requirements. Marissa will run the benchmark jobs.

Best,
Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: recommended shortlist + runbook (notes)

Internal notes — do not forward yet to Acme until we finalize the canary plan.

Recommended evaluation priority (internal):
1) Redwood-Open-7B-quant (Variant A) — prioritize for rerank + low-cost chat shadowing. Owner: Marissa. Deliverable: benchmark CSV + per-route latency breakdown by Wed 26 May.
2) Redwood-13B-std (Variant B) — validate multi-turn chat and hallucination rate. Owner: Sean. Deliverable: qualitative report on coherence/error modes by Fri 28 May.
3) Community-70B (Variant C) — run only if B shows material gap on multi-turns; otherwise deprioritize. Owner: Karthik (on hold).

Runbook highlights:
- Use the attached acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl as the canonical prompt set. Add synthetic context-length variations for stress testing.
- Quality gates: top-1 precision threshold for rerank (72%); hallucination rate < 6% for chat categories mapped to critical flows.
- Batching: prioritize small-batch (<8) latency tests to reflect user-facing flows; also run a throughput test config for dedicated sizing.

Action items and owners:
- Marissa: start benchmark runs and upload CSV to shared drive (due Wed 26 May).
- Sean: prep long-form chat eval and error taxonomy (due Fri 28 May).
- Karthik: schedule technical deep-dive with Acme and prepare procurement/committed-rate stub (due Mon 24 May).

Risks to flag:
- If Acme insists on model C for long-context summaries, cost could exceed their current budget; plan a fallback where we propose a hybrid pipeline (rerank + extractive for long docs).
- Security artifacts: they’ll likely ask for SOC2 + retention policies during procurement — have CS/Security ready.

Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
